title: Open-site cohomology comparisons and Zariski vanishing detection
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $T_\tau$ either its small etale or its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using small representatives in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A_T$ denote the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_\tau,A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^a$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be any set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$.
For every open $U\subseteq T$, the functor $(V\to U)\mapsto(V\to T,V\to U)$ identifies $U_\tau$ with the localized site $T_\tau/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], including its topology. Under this identification there is a canonical ring isomorphism $A_U\cong A_T|_U$, the identity on constant sections, and restriction of module sheaves is the exact sectionwise functor $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to T)$. These identifications respect iterated open restriction. The family $(U_i\to T)$ is a cover on $T_\tau$, and for every object $V\to T$ its pullback $(V\times_T U_i\to V)$ is a cover on $V_\tau$ and on the corresponding localized site.
Writing $r_U$ for this exact restriction and $D(r_U)$ for its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], there are canonical isomorphisms
$$\chi^a_{U,K}:r_U\mathcal H^a(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^a(D(r_U)K)$$
for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D(T_\tau,A)$. They are induced by the kernel, image and quotient comparisons, are natural for all derived morphisms, and agree with the composite comparisons for nested opens. For every module sheaf $F$ one has $F=0$ if and only if $r_{U_i}F=0$ for every $i$. Consequently, for every integer $a$,
$$\mathcal H^a(K)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal H^a(D(r_{U_i})K)=0\text{ for every }i.$$
These assertions include $T=\varnothing$ and the empty covering family; in that case every module sheaf is zero.

proof.text: Use the concrete inverse slice equivalences for both small sites and their dense-subsite covering equivalence. The composition functors preserve underlying schemes and structure maps; a private generic slice-inverse composition lemma proves the nested-open equality from homOfLE_ι and associativity, using extensionality of the underlying scheme and slice arrows. The continuity and cocontinuity interfaces from [lem-pur-open-small-ringed-site-coherence] give constant-sheafification compatibility over CommRingCat. Its unit equation proves normalization, and uniqueness of maps out of the sheafification proves compatibility with nested restriction. The module restrictions are the existing overFunctor and overMap: section formulas and the successive-restriction isomorphism are identities. Additivity is sectionwise, finite limits are reflected by the faithful presheaf functor, and overMap preserves finite colimits as a left adjoint.

proof.text: Specialize [lem-pur-zariski-cover-slice-module-detection] to the constant commutative ring sheaf. Its two cases give the base covering sieve (generating the pro-etale sieve from its covering presieve) and the exact zero-module detection equivalence. Pullback stability gives the displayed categorical pullback families, and the over-topology equivalence gives their slice coverings. Apply the base-cover result to the inverse-image opens on each object to obtain the third covering clause. For an empty scheme, apply module detection to the empty-index open family.

Apply the second clause of [lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence] to restriction to U, further restriction to W, restriction directly to W, and the existing sectionwise overFunctorMap isomorphism. Its equation is exactly cohomology_nested, with the displayed derivedNestedIso; no boundedness or resolution assumption is introduced.

proof.text: For fixed $a$, Step 2 applied to $F=\mathcal H^a(K)$ gives $\mathcal H^a(K)=0$ exactly when every $r_{U_i}\mathcal H^a(K)$ is zero. The isomorphisms of Step 3 identify these with $\mathcal H^a(D(r_{U_i})K)$. This proves the final equivalence; the empty case was already included in Step 2.
